verses.text: Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam, and Shemuel. They were heads of their families in the clan of Tola, and brave warriors. In David's time, the number of their descendants listed in the records was twenty-two thousand six hundred.
Uzzi's son was Izrahiah. Izrahiah's sons were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. All five of them were chiefs.
Their family records show that they had thirty-six thousand men ready for war, because they had many wives and children.
Their relatives among all the clans of Issachar were brave warriors. In all, eighty-seven thousand were listed in the family records.
Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.
Bela had five sons: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. They were heads of their families and brave warriors. Their family records listed twenty-two thousand and thirty-four fighting men.
Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were Becher's sons.
Their family records listed the heads of their families and twenty thousand two hundred brave warriors.
Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these descendants of Jediael were heads of families. They had seventeen thousand two hundred brave warriors ready to go to war.
Shuppim and Huppim were the sons of Ir, and Hushim was the son of Aher.
Naphtali's sons were Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were descendants of Bilhah.
Manasseh's descendants were Asriel, whose mother was his Aramean concubine. She also gave birth to Machir, the father of Gilead.
Machir took a wife from the families of Huppim and Shuppim. His sister was named Maacah. Another descendant was named Zelophehad, and he had only daughters.
Machir's wife Maacah gave birth to a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rakem.
Ulam's son was Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, the son of Manasseh.
Gilead's sister Hammolecheth gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
Ephraim's descendants were his son Shuthelah, Shuthelah's son Bered, Bered's son Tahath, Tahath's son Eleadah, Eleadah's son Tahath,
Tahath's son Zabad, and Zabad's son Shuthelah. Ephraim's sons Ezer and Elead were killed by the men of Gath who were born in that land, when they went down to steal the people's cattle.
Their father Ephraim mourned for them a long time, and his relatives came to comfort him.
Then he slept with his wife again, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. He named him Beriah, because trouble had come to his family.
Ephraim's daughter was Sheerah. She built Lower and Upper Beth Horon, and Uzzen Sheerah.
Beriah's descendants were his son Rephah, Rephah's son Resheph, Resheph's son Telah, Telah's son Tahan,
Tahan's son Ladan, Ladan's son Ammihud, Ammihud's son Elishama,
Elishama's son Nun, and Nun's son Joshua.
Their lands and settlements included Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages, as far as Azzah and its villages.
Along the borders of Manasseh were Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, with their villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these towns.
Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and of their sister Shua.
Japhlet's sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were Japhlet's sons.
Shomer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.
The sons of his brother Helem were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
Zophah's sons were Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
Jether's sons were Jephunneh, Pispa, and Ara.
Ulla's sons were Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.
All these were descendants of Asher. They were heads of families, the best and bravest warriors, and outstanding leaders. Their family records listed twenty-six thousand men ready for war.
